Minor, 16:9, t≈0.40–0.44: three documents overlap each other and the filter frame at once. DOC-13 is waiting, DOC-12 is inside the glass, and DOC-11 is exiting partly behind the right post and under the lever. Fix: space the documents so each one clears the filter before the next one enters.
Minor: the jurisdiction name chips on the documents are about 11–12 px at 1080p. The seal glyphs carry the identity, but a larger seal and chip would help on mobile.
LAW-0070: Connector labels cover their own connectors (reviewer defect #5). At 16:9, the 'different from the key' chip (≈135 px) sits on a ≈145 px connector, so only about 7 px of line shows on each side. 'passes through' leaves short stubs too, and so does ES 'distinta de la clave'. In long-labels, the 'sets the key of the filter' chip hides the dashed card→filter connector completely, with no arrowhead visible. Fix: lengthen these connectors by spacing the filter, trays and card further apart, or add the connector corridors to relationGraph obstacles so the labels are pushed aside onto leaders (as LAW-0442 does).

The outlet arrows do not land. At 9:16 (t≥0.45), the 'same as the key' and 'different from the key' arrowheads stop 40–70 px above the trays, in empty space. They also start at points on the filter's bottom edge that are not the two dark outlet ports drawn there. At 16:9, the 'different from the key' arrowhead stops about 15 px short of the Other tray. Fix: route the outlet connectors from the drawn ports to the tray edges, using custom from/to anchors.

Truncation removes meaning. The filter window's second label is cut to 'declared on the…' in 9:16 and to 'declarada en el…' in ES, which is one of the two values being compared. Fix: use 2 lines, or place the label under the window where there is room.
long-labels-stress: the source document's declared jurisdiction wraps mid-word as 'Northvale-upo / n-Eastmere'. Fix: break at the hyphen or shrink the text.

The tracer collides with labels. At t≈0.47, the tracer icon covers the 'holds' chip. At t≈0.55–0.60, the tracer sits over 'key from the card' / 'declared on the document' inside the enlarged filter during the comparison beat. Fix: offset the tracer's path through the filter below the window labels, and route it off the chip on the 'holds' leg.
ES, 16:9: the 'contiene' relation chip touches the 'Documento de origen' name chip, so the two read as one label group. Fix: separate them, or move the element name below the document as in 9:16.

Logic: at the end, DOC-11 is still drawn at full strength in its source position while a copy also lands in the Relevant tray, so the traced document appears in two places. Fix: dim or outline the source position once the traced copy departs, or make it explicit that the marker is a copy.
LAW-0071: 9:16, all times: the two stacked panels use only about 64% of the caption-safe width (in a 700 px cell, about 395 of 613 px, x≈150–545 with about 100 px empty on each side). The library, gate and document are small as a result (the document is about 70 px wide). The references fill 85–90% of the width (LAW-0443, LAW-0683). Cause: the portrait STAGES {w:860, h:640} ×2 plus headers and gap is taller than the 900×1400 design space, so everything is scaled down. Fix: use a shorter portrait panel stage (e.g. about 860×470, with the card beside the gate rather than above it) so that the stacked panels span the full width.

The one consequence that only A shows, its reference written on the card, is a line of text about 6–7 px high in the render (about 10 px at 1080p). With textVisibility 'none' it disappears completely, and the A and B cards are identical at t=1. Fix: draw a visible graphic mark on A's card, such as a filled slot strip, a tick, or a small document thumbnail pinned to the card, and make it large enough to read at 1080p.

1:1, t≥0.4: in both panels the library is drawn as an empty brown cabinet with no row of books, so the 'biblioteca' reading is lost in the square layout. Fix: keep a row of books visible in the square library.
Minor, 9:16: the 'Same facts: Same document · Same research card · Same gate' chip wraps to leave 'gate' alone on the second line. Fix: widen the chip or shorten the text for portrait.
LAW-0072: 16:9, t≈0.78–0.84, in both baseline and long-labels: as the lens folds back, the enlarged copy overlaps the '≠ Other jurisdiction' chip (clipping it to 'Other jurisdictio') and the cabinet's right frame. The long-labels chip 'Declares another jurisdiction' is overlapped the same way. Fix: fold the lens along a path that stays clear of the compartment chips (for example, straight down onto the document from above), or treat the chip boxes as obstacles for the lens's intermediate positions.

long-labels-stress, t≈0.35–0.75: the lens, the element that exists to show the declaration, breaks the inspected value mid-word as 'Northvale-upo / n-Eastmere'. Fix: break at the hyphen, shrink the text to a minimum size, or widen the declaration box in the lens.

textVisibility 'none', t≈0.60–0.75: the 'chip-arrow' group (the line and arrowhead between the Before and After chips, LAW-0072.js lines 237–239 and 374) is still built and shown while both chips are hidden, leaving a '↓' floating in empty space to the right of the cabinet. Fix: build or show the arrow only when chipsOn is true.

Minor: the old slot's ghost is a thin, faint dashed outline. It is hard to see at mobile size and nearly invisible with labels hidden, which weakens 'keep the before value traceable'. Fix: use a heavier dash or a light tinted fill for the ghost slot.

Minor, 1:1, t=1: the 'Datum changed: Northvale → Eastmere' chip sits above the cabinet on a diagonal leader of about 260 px across the Other compartment. Fix: place the chip closer to the marked document.

LAW-0073: [latest review verdict pass but ID not accepted: re-verify; no specific defects recorded]

Non-blocking, 1:1 (all times): the wall-shelf library shrinks to a thin strip. Its S1/S2/S3 spine tags are about 5 px at 1080p and cannot be read, so the 'library as anchor' reads weakly. Fix: give the square shelf about 150 design px (SHAPES.square.libH) or enlarge the tagged volumes.
Non-blocking, 16:9 long-labels-stress: the bookcase plaque 'Reference library — ground floor' shrinks to about 12 px at 1080p. Fix: allow the plaque to wrap to 2 lines or widen it past the bookcase.

Non-blocking wrap orphans: 'Letter from Party / A' on the S1 sheet (16:9 and 1:1); the 1:1 hold callout 'No source has been supplied for this row / yet'. Fix: balance the line breaks or widen the chip.
LAW-0074: The key change has no physical source (all ratios, t≈0.615→0.63 at 16:9). The pin appears from nothing: opacity steps 0→1 at scale 1.35, 40 px above the cell, then drops into the socket (frame(): nodes['cell-pin'] opacity pinP>0?1:0, T(cellC.x, cellC.y-40*(1-drop))). Nothing carries it from the card's gold grommet or down the column. Fix: have the pin ride from the proposition card's grommet along the 'row' connector into the socket when the tracer arrives, or slide it down the 'column' connector from the sheet, keeping it visible the whole way.

The tracer is nearly invisible. It is a ~10 px red dot that runs under the elements and under the 'holds'/'column' chips. In the 9:16 strip t=0.46–0.73 it is visible in only 3 of 10 frames (0.52, 0.58, 0.61); at 16:9 t=0.60 it is half hidden under the 'column' chip. The brief's beat 'mover un marcador de seguimiento por las relaciones' does not read. Fix: use a larger marker (≥22 px) drawn above the connectors, and keep relation labels off its path.

Connectors are too short and covered by their own labels (all ratios). 'holds' (shelf→sheet, ~70 px at 16:9) and 'column' (sheet→cell, ~65 px) each have the chip in the middle, leaving ~15 px stubs. In long-labels-stress 16:9 t=1, the 'row of this proposition' chip fills the entire card→cell connector and shrinks to ~13 px at 1080p. Fix: increase the vertical gaps between shelf, sheet and cell, and place relation labels beside the connector with a short leader. Do not shrink relation labels below ~20 px at 1080p.

9:16 layout collisions (t≥0.12): the dashed 'Pending source' column header touches the S1 source sheet with zero gap, and the dotted leader of 'leads to the shelf' runs along the left edge of the 'Library shelf' chip. Fix: move the pending header right or below with a clear gap, and route the leader outside the chip.
Minor: the search query in the long-labels preset shrinks to ~10 px in the printout (16:9 t=1). The card 'Party A sent written notice on Day / 3.' leaves an orphan '3.' on a wide card at 16:9.
LAW-0075: The red comparison ring in scenario A cuts through the 'entry 14' pinpoint flag in the held final state, in every ratio from t=0.78. At 16:9 the ring crosses the '4'; at 9:16 the 'e'; at 1:1 the '4'. In long-labels it crosses 'entry 14-15'. Fix: when the ring is shown, move the flag to the free side of the cell (or out of the ring radius), or draw the ring as a bracket that avoids the flag box.

Scenario B's 'S2 · Source pending' sticky note fades in on top of the slot's own 'S2' id and dashed page icon (16:9 t≈0.24–0.28, visible at t=0.26). This is a garbled cross-fade, and the note appears from nowhere instead of being placed. Fix: fade the slot id out (lifting it) before the note appears. Better, drop or slap the note in from above the board so it lands fully opaque.

long-labels-stress 16:9 t=1: the S-002 sheet title is truncated to 'Warehouse delivery log, loading dock B…', so meaning is lost. The column-head pins sit on the last character of 'S-001'/'S-002'. The shelf strip drops to 62% height, making the S-001/S-002 spine tags illegible. The 'Changed fact: proposition 2 × source S-002' chip touches the neutral note with zero gap and overlaps the corner of panel B. Fix: allow 3 lines on sheet titles and move the head pin clear of the id text. Keep the shelf height, or scale the tag font with it. Add a gap between the guide chip and the neutral note.
Minor, 1:1: proposition cards wrap to 4 lines with orphans ('7.'), so the boards feel cramped. Consider narrower grid columns and wider cards in the square layout.
LAW-0076: The enlarged detail does not show what is being inspected (all ratios, t=0.35–0.76). The lens crops the focus row so the proposition card is a blank ~20–60 px sliver with no text. The cited column head (S1 'Letter from Party A') is not in the lens, and ~60% of the lens is empty trailing columns (S2, S3, pending fill). At 16:9 the magnification is only ~1.6× the full-size context row. Fix: frame the lens on the card text + cited cell + column head, and crop or collapse the empty columns so the pin, thread and flag are enlarged ≥2.5×.

The dashed lens leaders run across the thumbnail's card text (16:9 t=0.3–0.8: left leader through the row 2/3 cards; 9:16 t=0.43/0.72: through 'reached the' and 'Party B asked'; long-labels: through row 3). Fix: start the leaders from the focus-rect corners on the outside, route them around the thumbnail, or draw them beneath it.

When the pin returns to the card inside the lens, it sits on the lens's left red border (16:9 t=0.6–0.75, 9:16 t=0.72, 1:1 t=0.72) and looks clipped by the window. Fix: include more of the card inside the lens so the pin's resting point has clearance from the frame.
The 'Source pending' note fades in inside the lens (t≈0.60–0.65) and appears from nowhere. Fix: slide it in from the pending column head or from outside the lens edge, fully opaque.

long-labels-stress 16:9 t=0.66: the new flag 'entry 16 (loading dock C)' and the struck 'entry 14-15 (loading dock B)' stack against the lens top edge. The S3 column line runs through both flags, and the new flag's pole crosses the struck flag's text. Fix: place the flags below the row line or wrap them to 2 lines inside the focus cell, keep clearance from column lines, and offset the new flag's pole.

LAW-0077: 9:16, t=0.34-0.46 (all presets): the right forearm sweeps across the citation-trail card on its way to the book cradle and hides the card's middle and right column ('Journal of S…', 'Treatise on Sa…', 'Note 12 / p. 88 / fol. 14') while row 2 is being recorded (row1 window 0.42-0.46). Fix: in bayPlacement('portrait'), move the cradle or shoulder, or use a different bend side, so the arm's path clears the card's box. Alternatively add the card box to the arm-path obstacle check and keep the card above the arm layer only while it is recording.

Alternative preset (intermediate-only), 16:9, t=0.48-0.52: the right arm withdraws and the stage window cuts it at the wrist, so only a brown hand bump is left on the bottom edge of the stage. Fix: retract along a path that keeps forearm and hand visible together until both are below the window edge, or fade the hand with the forearm.

9:16 long-labels-stress, t=1: three labels crowd the top-right. The 'Intermediate reference' chip sits on the second chain (about x 1100, y 620 in the 700-px cell), and the vertical leader of 'The card records each stop of the trail in order' runs across the chain and the archive box down to the card. Fix: add the chain samples and the box as labelPlacer obstacles in portrait, and route that leader to the card's left or top edge.

16:9 long-labels-stress, t=1: the actor label 'Research assistant checking the reference' is drawn over the right forearm near the bottom edge. Fix: add the solved armPath as an obstacle when placing the actor label, or anchor the label at the left edge of the bottom-right corner.

16:9 and 1:1, t=0.50-0.58: the forearm covers the 'Archive · HB' plate as the hand reaches into the box ('Archi…' visible). This is minor, but the plate identifies the box. Fix: put the plate on the box's left half or lower it.

All ratios, t>=0.57 hold: the forearm crosses in front of the lifted original and covers its right edge and the seal; in 9:16 it covers about a third of the folio. Fix: grip the folio by its right edge or lower corner so the arm stays outside the page, or raise the page to the left of the hand.
LAW-0078: All ratios, t>=0.18 through the hold: the relation connectors ('holds' shelf→treatise, 'locates the shelf' terminal→shelf, 'records' article→card) end in dots about 10-25 design px short of both elements, floating in empty space. The brief's acceptanceCheck is that each connector ends on its element. Cause: LAW-0078.js lines 199-201 anchor to inflate(box, maxAmp + 0.02) plus pad 4, which is the box sized for the enlarged focus state. Fix: anchor with edgeAnchor on the element's actual box at its current scale (recompute per frame, or inflate only while that element is enlarged), with pad 0-2.

9:16, t>=0.30 through the hold: the second chain (treatise footnote → source entry) drops vertically down the folio's left margin. It overprints the folio heading ('fol. 14', 'Minute book of the', 'Harbour Board', 'Day 12 · Year 1') and the entry numbers 1-3 (see crop-0078-p-chain.png). Fix: in the portrait layout, offset the folio so the chain arrives from the left, outside the page, and hooks the eyelet in the entry's left margin; or route the chain around the page edge with a side port.

9:16: the 'cites' and 'holds' chips sit side by side at the same height (about y 540), and 'holds' is about 45 px from its connector, so it is ambiguous which relation each labels. Fix: place each relation label at its own connector's midpoint (graph.js relation-label placement with obstacles and separateLabels).

16:9 long-labels-stress, t=1: the element label 'Library catalogue search terminal' sits about 95 px below the terminal, next to the source folio's label, and 'Citation-trail record card' sits about 120 px right of the card. Both are detached. The 'records' connector's end dot also lands inside the card header beside 'Citation trail'. Fix: anchor element labels to their own element's free edge and re-anchor the connector to the grown card box.
LAW-0079: Panel A, all ratios and presets, including labels hidden: the right arm reaches the box lid (0.18-0.31), leaves the panel entirely while the lid stays open (lidBack 0.31-0.38, absent until about 0.53), then re-enters to lift the folio. On entry and exit the panel window cuts it at the wrist, leaving a detached brown hand bump on the panel's bottom border at t about 0.18-0.22 and 0.50-0.56 (16:9 t=0.20 and 0.55; 9:16 t=0.55). Fix: keep the hand on the box rim or lid between opening and lifting (no exit), or clip hand and forearm together so no lone hand shows.

Key recorded difference illegible: in panel B the card's row 3 annotation 'as cited in Treatise on Sample Remedies, p. 88' renders at about 6 px in a 1920-wide 16:9 frame. The card rows are about 9-10 px, and in 1:1 row 3 truncates to 'Minute book of the Harbour…'. The closing guide says 'Two ways of recording the same citation', but the recording itself cannot be read. Fix: crop each panel to the region that changes (treatise → box → card), or add a per-panel enlarged card or row-3 inset so this text is at least about 18 px at 1080p. Give row 3 two lines instead of an ellipsis in 1:1.

The whole story bay, including the catalogue terminal, note board and shelf, is shrunk to about 40% per panel, so almost all in-scene text is 7-10 px at 1080p. Consider dropping the terminal and note board from the panels, which are identical in A and B and already stated by the 'Same facts' note, to enlarge the box, folio and card.

The catalogue query never appears in either panel: the input field is empty for the whole animation except a stray 2-px sliver of the first glyph. LAW-0079 never passes `type`/`result` to stage.pose, so the kit's qclip width stays at 4 px (kit line 1259), and editing the `query` field has no visible effect. Fix: include type:1, result:1 in vA/vB.
16:9 and 9:16, t=0.24-0.32: the forearm covers the 'Archive' plate of box A while opening the lid (minor).
LAW-0080: All ratios, t=0-1: the context view's catalogue terminal shows an empty search field containing only a stray 2-px sliver of the first glyph (crop-0080-query.png), with the result row unlit. The 'build' beat is meant to show the state produced by the trail, yet the query that found the treatise is missing, and the `query` field has no visible effect. Cause: stage.pose in LAW-0080 (lines 112 and 349) never sets `type`/`result`, so the kit's qclip stays at 4 px. Fix: add type:1, result:1 to the base pose.

Content ambiguity in the default preset: the treatise's own footnote number (innerNote '3', printed as the highlighted superscript '3' on the treatise page and in its footnote) equals the substituted datum 'entry 3'. After the swap to 'entry 2', a highlighted '3' remains in the treatise, and viewers can read it as the old entry value. Fix: give LAW-0080 presets an innerNote that differs from beforeValue and afterValue (for example '7').

Minor, 16:9 t about 0.62-0.68: the incoming 'entry 2' tag fades in semi-transparently over the bookshelf spines, which reduces contrast while it appears. Consider an opaque card backing, or place the before/after pair over the dimmed counter area. The timing matches accepted LAW-0444, so this is not blocking.
